name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Memory Provenance Laundering in LLM Agents: A Non-Amplification Firewall for Persistent Memory
items.dek: Memory consolidation in LLM agents can launder untrusted observations into trusted context; a provenance-preserving firewall blocks unauthorized tool calls.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to fixed risk policies and schema-grounded settings; generalization to production agent architectures and mixed-trust memory sources untested.

items.title: Tailscale didn't stop the Hugging Face intrusion
items.dek: Hugging Face intrusion proceeded despite Tailscale deployment, indicating VPN alone insufficient for supply-chain protection.
items.unproven: whether Tailscale was misconfigured, what the actual attack vector was, or how this generalizes beyond this incident

items.title: AgenticRepair: Multi-Faceted Program Context Engineering for Agentic Vulnerability Repair
items.dek: Agentic LLM system achieves 73% success on vulnerability repair by engineering multi-source program context; applicability to reader's SDLC unclear.
items.unproven: evaluated on SEC-Bench only; no evidence on SAST rule findings or real triage workflows; unclear whether sanitizer-verified patches meet production security standards.

items.title: RFC 10015: Deprecating Obsolete Key Exchange Methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2
items.dek: RFC 10015 proposes deprecating obsolete key exchange methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2.
items.unproven: does not establish timeline for enforcement or impact on legacy systems the reader must support

items.title: On fair and realistic performance evaluations for graph-based lateral movement detectors
items.dek: Benchmark study shows lateral movement detector evaluations vary widely by preprocessing and labeling; affects threat hunting, not application security.
items.unproven: reader does not own threat detection or hunting infrastructure; findings inform research rigor but do not change SDLC or architecture review decisions.

items.title: MOSAIC: Masked Outsourcing of Secure AI Computations
items.dek: Protocol for secure outsourced AI inference with acceptable transformer perplexity; interesting but no evidence of deployment or adoption.
items.unproven: single implementation on 70B models; no field use; reader concerned with agents in SDLC, not external inference outsourcing; unclear threat model vs. existing model quantization.

items.title: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
items.dek: GUI agents degrade under multi-turn persuasion despite single-turn guardrails; relevant to agent SDLC security but limited to mobile setting.
items.unproven: tested on three frontier models; no evidence on agents in reader's software pipeline; escalation patterns may not transfer to backend or API agent deployments.

items.title: Harvesting SSH Credentials: Insights from My Honeypot Network
items.dek: Honeypot data characterizes SSH credential theft patterns; no novel attack method.
items.unproven: generalization beyond the operator's network and threat model

items.title: Scanning 7.6 Petabytes of HuggingFace Training Data for Secrets
items.dek: Truffle Security scanned HuggingFace data for exposed secrets; found many, no novel detection method disclosed.
items.unproven: Whether findings represent actual exploitable credentials versus false positives; no methodology for remediation or impact assessment provided.

items.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
items.dek: Online shadow tomography algorithm matches classical adaptive-data-analysis bounds for quantum state measurement.
items.unproven: Quantum theory; outside reader's domain.

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.dek: Sample complexity lower bound for quantum spectrum and entropy estimation scales as Ω(d²⁻ᵞ).
items.unproven: Quantum information theory; not applicable to reader's SDLC or agent security work.

items.title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
items.dek: Kikuchi hierarchy achieves sharp planted-signal trade-off for kXOR without polylogarithmic loss.
items.unproven: Complexity theory; no bearing on application security tooling or software supply-chain decisions.

items.title: StraightDP: Geometry-Aware Differential Privacy for Rectified-Flow Transformers
items.dek: Differential privacy for generative models exploits geometry of rectified flows to mitigate utility cliffs under strong privacy budgets.
items.unproven: Single architecture (transformers) and dataset (MNIST); scaling and applicability to large production models not demonstrated.

items.title: Rooting, firmware analysis and persistent credentials of TP-Link TL-841N
items.dek: TP-Link TL-841N firmware analysis extracts hardcoded credentials and rooting technique.
items.unproven: applicability beyond this specific model; whether credentials are reused across product lines; relevance to current firmware versions in production

items.title: Show HN: Bor – Open-source policy management for Linux desktops
items.dek: Open-source Linux desktop policy management tool with mTLS/gRPC delivery; version 0.8 adds Thunderbird and FirewallD support.
items.unproven: no evidence of deployment at scale, no comparative analysis against existing EDR or MDM tooling, no threat model or security audit published

items.title: CWEEP: A Lexical Static Analysis Framework for CWE Early Prevention
items.dek: Static analysis for RTL hardware security reaches 60.8% precision on synthetic bug datasets; outside application security scope.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to manually inserted bugs and LLM-generated code; no real production RTL or comparison to manual review; reader does not work in hardware design.

items.title: Quantum computing-based solver for interacting power grids
items.dek: Quantum hybrid solver for power grid resonance analysis; quantum computing application unrelated to SDLC or secure code review.
items.unproven: Validated on single 5-bus system only; no evidence this scales to production grids or outperforms classical approaches in practice.

items.title: Beyond Resilience: Antifragility in Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity
items.dek: Theory and measurement of antifragility in industrial control systems; reader manages software security, not OT infrastructure.
items.unproven: findings drawn from event databases and one hardware testbed; does not establish operational guidance for application security teams.

items.title: Bending the Curve: Operational Cyber Epidemiology for Ransomware
items.dek: SEIR epidemiology model applied to ransomware incident management and SOC decision support; reader does not run security operations.
items.unproven: framework is conceptual; no evidence from active incident response, no operational SOC deployment, no data showing R0/Re improve decision quality.

items.title: Enforcing Cryptographic Distributed-VCS Access Control with No Trust on Servers
items.dek: Attribute-based encryption scheme for distributed VCS access control without central server; cryptographic design not relevant to SDLC tooling.
items.unproven: no performance benchmarks, no usability study, no comparison to current VCS (Git, GitLab) access models that are already sufficient for most teams.

items.title: Anti-fraud tools can't keep pace with robocall scammers
items.dek: Anti-fraud tools lag robocall sophistication; systemic detection gap known and outside application security scope.
items.unproven: whether presented evidence is new measurement or existing reporting of known arms race

items.title: On the Resilience of 5G NR Against Jamming
items.dek: Simulation study of 5G NR jamming resilience shows channel bandwidth and frequency matter most; outside reader's remit.
items.unproven: ns-3 simulation only; no field validation; reader does not design or audit wireless infrastructure.

items.title: JUNO: Aggregated Vector Consensus for Optimal Asynchronous Common Subset
items.dek: Consensus protocol achieves O(n²) message complexity with 93% throughput gain over HoneyBadgerBFT; distributed systems theory, not application security.
items.unproven: reader does not build or operate blockchain or BFT systems; evaluation is algorithmic, not relevant to SDLC or secure architecture.

items.title: Californians' data deletion requests, DROP, become enforceable Aug. 1
items.dek: California data deletion law becomes enforceable August 1.

items.title: EU rules on AI models become enforceable. What's going to change?
items.dek: EU AI Act enforcement timeline and regulatory scope summary.

noise.title: Algorithms on billion-scale graph using 10GB RAM: I love DataFusion
noise.dek: Engineering blog post on using DataFusion for graph processing demonstrates a tool capability, not a security finding.

noise.title: Postmortem for Kernel Soundness Bug #14576
noise.dek: Post-mortem of a kernel bug in Lean theorem prover; outside application security engineering scope.
noise.unproven: not relevant to SAST/DAST/SCA tooling, secure SDLC processes, or AI/post-quantum security in the reader's domain

noise.title: Danube's record low levels force shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear plant
noise.dek: Hungarian nuclear plant shut down due to low Danube water levels; infrastructure news unrelated to application security.
